Alright, the recent steps: I appended a journal entry, verified everything is committed, then tried to run the end-to-end test `test_full_pipeline_end_to_end`. I launched it in the background with a timeout of 600 seconds, redirecting output to `/tmp/pipe_probe.log`, and printed "started". The command returned immediately with "started", meaning the test is now running asynchronously.

Next, I attempted to peek at the log after 45 seconds using a separate `sleep 30; tr ...` command, but the tool blocked me because chaining `sleep` with other commands is disallowed. The system gave a specific suggestion: use a `Monitor` with an until-loop, or use `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands. I need to respect that.

My goal now is to monitor the progress of the e2e probe. I don't know exactly how long it will take, but I can check the size of the log file to see if any substantial output has been written. A size threshold of a few kilobytes (say >2000 bytes) should indicate that the test has produced some output we can inspect. Once the size exceeds that, I can safely read the last few lines of the log.

So I should construct a Bash command that loops until the file size grows beyond 2000 bytes, sleeping a few seconds between checks, then after the condition is met, dump the last 10 lines of the log (with CR to newline conversion and filtering out empty lines). This fits the allowed pattern: a single command with an `until` loop and a final `tr ... | tail`. I also need to set a generous timeout (e.g., 120 seconds) to give the test enough time to produce output without risking a premature cutoff.

Thus, the appropriate tool call is:

```json
{
  "command": "until [ $(stat -c %s /tmp/pipe_probe.log) -gt 2000 ]; do sleep 5; done; tr '\\r' '\\n' < /tmp/pipe_probe.log | grep . | tail -10",
  "description": "Wait for probe output",
  "timeout": 120000
}
```

This will wait until the log is >2000 bytes, then show the most recent lines. That should give me insight into whether the e2e test is hanging, progressing, or has completed. I’ll issue this as the next tool call.
